recent_posts.title: Categorize Your Dependencies
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the limitations of using dependencies and devDependencies in npm, suggesting a more flexible approach to categorizing dependencies in projects using pnpm catalogs. It introduces various dependency categories beyond production and development, enhancing version management and project maintainability. The post also highlights tooling support for pnpm catalogs and envisions future integration possibilities to improve developer experience.

recent_posts.title: Hello Tokyo!
recent_posts.summary: Seven years after an inspiring trip to Japan, the author fulfills a long-held desire to live there. Now in Tokyo, they recount the initial experiences of settling in, attending meetups, and embracing the cultural and lifestyle changes. They express gratitude for the support from friends and colleagues that made the transition possible. The post highlights the challenges and joys of starting new life chapters in a different country.

recent_posts.title: Photos Page
recent_posts.summary: A frontend developer shares the creation of a personal photos page on their website, moving away from Instagram due to recent changes. Utilizing skills in web development, the author downloaded and processed their Instagram data, preserving memories and building a custom platform to share their photos.

recent_posts.title: Async, Sync, in Between
recent_posts.summary: In programming, handling both synchronous (sync) and asynchronous (async) functions often leads to the 'coloring problem', where a function's asynchronous or synchronous nature affects the entire codebase. This post introduces 'quansync', a new approach to decouple code from the coloring problem by allowing functions to be used as both sync and async based on context. Examples showcase how quansync can simplify code without duplicating logic, improving flexibility while managing async dependencies.

recent_posts.title: Move on to ESM-only
recent_posts.summary: Modern tools and libraries have increasingly adopted ESM as the primary module format, reducing the need for dual CJS/ESM packages. Transitioning to ESM-only simplifies development, reduces maintenance overhead, and improves package optimization. While careful consideration is needed when moving legacy packages, new packages should be released as ESM-only to leverage the benefits of modern tooling. The gradual adoption of ESM in the ecosystem is evident, and tools like Node Modules Inspector help in analyzing dependencies for a smoother transition.

recent_posts.title: Epoch Semantic Versioning
recent_posts.summary: Epoch Semantic Versioning introduces a more granular way to communicate changes in software versions. Instead of traditional semantic versioning, which uses major, minor, and patch versions, it adds an epoch number to signify significant changes. This approach aims to make it easier for users to understand the scale of changes and to adopt updates progressively.

recent_posts.title: CPU Profiling Nuxt
recent_posts.summary: To debug the bundling performance of your Nuxt app, use Node.js to generate CPU profiles instead of the `nuxi dev` command. Using `node --cpu-prof` and specifying the direct path to the CLI in `node_modules`, along with `--fork=false`, is necessary. After stopping the Nuxt process, find the generated `CPU.***.cpuprofile` files in your working directory and visualize them using CPUpro or a VS Code extension for easier access.

recent_posts.title: Initiative on Sponsorship Forwarding
recent_posts.summary: Open-source projects require support and funding for sustainability. Front-facing projects and high-profile maintainers often receive more attention and sponsorships than underlying dependencies and low-profile maintainers. The post discusses the unbalanced funding and proposes solutions, such as sponsorships forwarding on GitHub and Open Collective. The author also introduces their personal collective as an initiative to redistribute funds to dependencies and contributors. Transparency and fairness in fund distribution are emphasized.

recent_posts.title: Refreshed Nuxt ESLint Integrations
recent_posts.summary: Explore the refreshed Nuxt ESLint integrations and learn how to integrate ESLint with Nuxt for improved code quality.

recent_posts.title: Introducing ESLint Config Inspector
recent_posts.summary: ESLint Config Inspector is a tool that helps in analyzing and understanding ESLint configuration files. It provides insights into the rules and plugins used in the configuration, making it easier to manage and customize ESLint settings.

top_posts.title: Animated SVG Logo
top_posts.summary: The first time I saw such stroke animations in SVG is the Material Line Icons by Vjacheslav Trushkin. The animation is done by moving the dash on strokes, while my Logo is a vector outline with multiple control points. The only downside is that the stroke is evenly thick everywhere, making it looks less like a signature.
